subject: Decision support: inference hosting trade-offs & commercial ask
snippet: Recap from today: estimated 1M tokens/day, exploring Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private; requested tailored cost comparison and pilot pricing; next step: technical deep-dive.
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.example>
To: Jordan Li <jordan.li@acmedata.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.example>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.example>
Date: 2027-08-15T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Decision support: inference hosting trade-offs & commercial ask

Jordan — great to connect earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from today’s discovery so we have the same picture and can scope cost comparisons accurately.

What we heard on the call:
- Primary workload: interactive semantic search + short generative completions in product UI.
- Initial traffic estimate: ~1,000,000 tokens/day with expected ramp to ~10M tokens/day within 6 months if engagement grows.
- Latency/SLOs: target P95 < 120ms for UI queries, availability target 99.9%.
- Security: must run in a VPC for customer data isolation; SOC2 and basic audit logs required.

High-level deployment options to evaluate (we'll build a short cost model for each):
1) Hosted API (pay-as-you-go): simplest to start, per-token pricing. Good for low-friction onboarding, but can be more expensive at scale without discounts.
2) Dedicated (reserved GPU pool): predictable monthly commit with dedicated throughput; better unit economics for steady volume but requires commit and some lead time.
3) Private (VPC/on-prem): full isolation and control, one-time infra setup + licensing and ops overhead; best for strict compliance/regulatory needs.

Rough ballpark math we’ll refine in the model: (examples to aid conversation only)
- Hosted per-token: at $0.0006/token, 1M tokens/day => ~$600/day (~$18k/month).
- Dedicated commit: e.g., 4-GPU reserved pool ~$12k/month baseline (includes reserved throughput) + much lower incremental cost for bursts.
- Private/on-prem: CAPEX + OPEX (license + infra + ops) — initial setup + ~45k/month equivalent for small clusters (depends heavily on region/instance types).

Ask / next steps:
- Can you confirm the token distribution (approx % of queries under 50 tokens vs long >200 tokens) and expected peak QPS? This helps us pick GPU sizing and batching assumptions.
- I'll attach a mutual action plan (MAP) template and a short cost template. If you can fill traffic columns, we’ll run a tied comparison (per-token vs commit vs private) and return a recommendation plus pilot pricing.
- Recommend a technical deep-dive with Priyom (capacity and quantization) to validate model size and ops constraints — do you have availability next week?

Attachments: Acme-MAP-v1.xlsx, SOC2-overview.pdf (for quick compliance checklist).

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter | Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Acme-MAP-v1.xlsx]
[Attachment: SOC2-overview.pdf]

From: Jordan Li <jordan.li@acmedata.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.example>
Cc: procurement@acmedata.ai
Date: 2027-08-15T12:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Decision support: inference hosting trade-offs & commercial ask

Ben — thanks for the recap and the clear options. A few clarifications before you build the model:
- Traffic: 1M tokens/day is a safe baseline; realistic steady state may be 700k–1.2M, with 20% long-form queries (~200–800 tokens) and the remainder short (<50 tokens).
- Peak: we expect occasional spikes (~3–4x baseline) during promotions.
- Compliance: SOC2 is required; we'll also need IP whitelisting and 12-month audit logs retained.

Procurement ask: we are sensitive to large monthly commits given uncertain growth. Any model that reduces downside risk (pilot credits, conversion credits from Dedicated -> Private, or a stepped commit) would be favorable.

I’ve attached a brief doc with initial security reqs. Also please include a per-token vs commit sensitivity table that accounts for short vs long token mix — that will be the main input for our CFO.

Jordan
Jordan Li | Director, Product Ops | Acme Data
[Attachment: Initial-Security-Reqs.docx]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.example>

Date: 2027-08-16T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Decision support: inference hosting trade-offs & commercial ask

Jordan — got it, thanks. Attached is a lightweight model and an initial commercial proposal. Summary of the refined cost runs (assumptions: model ~7B parameters, typical request mix per your note):

1) Hosted (pay-as-you-go)
- Assumed blended rate with volume tiers: $0.00055/token at ~1M/day baseline -> ~$16.5k/month.
- Upside: no commit, easy to pilot; downside: can be more expensive at steady scale.

2) Dedicated (reserved pool + metered bursts) — sample structure
- Reserved pool (4x vGPU equivalent) commit: $9,800/month (covers baseline throughput ~1.1M tokens/day with our batching assumptions).
- Metered burst beyond baseline: $0.00012/token.
- Effective range: $9.8k–$13.5k/month depending on burst volume. Break-even vs hosted around ~1.2M tokens/day.

3) Private (VPC/on-prem)
- One-time onboarding + licensing: estimated $95k setup (networking, KMS, audit pipeline).
- Equivalent monthly TCO (amortized + ops): ~$36k–$50k/month depending on region and staffing. Good when you need full data residency and long-term cost control.

Pilot option we propose:
- 6-week Dedicated pilot with a 30% trial credit on the reserved commit and standard metered bursts.
- Option to convert pilot payments as credit toward Private onboarding if you decide to migrate within 90 days.

Next steps asked of Acme:
- Complete the MAP traffic columns in the attached MAP (Acme-MAP-v1.xlsx) and return — we’ll use that to run the exact sensitivity table (per-token vs commit tiers).
- Approve scheduling: Priyom for a deep-dive on model size, expected seq lengths, and quantization options (30–40% GPU footprint reduction likely).
- Procurement: if a stepped commit helps, we can draft a 3-month stepped commit with a review at month 3.

Attachments: Redwood-pilot-offer.pdf, cost-model.csv (attached with the runs).

Date: 2027-08-17T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Decision support: inference hosting trade-offs & commercial ask

Jordan / Ben — quick technical notes to prepare for the deep-dive:
- Region: please indicate preferred cloud region (us-west-2 / us-east-1 / eu-west-1). This materially affects instance types and pricing.
- Model size & SPM: confirm model family (7B vs 13B) and typical seq length distribution; we use that to size KV cache and GPU memory.
- Quantization: applying 4-bit quantization and optimized kernels typically reduces GPU footprint ~30–40% for dense gen; will influence whether 4-GPU reserved pool is required or 3 GPUs suffice.
- Integration: SSO/SCIM and KMS timelines — we typically need 2–3 weeks for SSO setup and 1 week for KMS key exchange.

If you can drop the model name and preferred region into the MAP sheet this morning, I’ll produce a refined capacity plan and updated cost rows by EOD tomorrow.

— Priyom
Priyom Das | Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
